steps.title: Write the rules for your agents (AGENTS.md)
steps.how: AGENTS.md is at the repo root, and a CLAUDE.md (at the root or in .claude/), when there is one, imports it (`@AGENTS.md`, or `@../AGENTS.md` from .claude/; a Markdown link is not an import): with a CLAUDE.md, Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only through it
steps.why: an agent follows the rules it can read, and only those

steps.title: Turn on the guard for your agents' commands
steps.how: .claude/settings.json has a PreToolUse hook that runs `yokoten hook`. With a .muse/hooks.json, Muse Code must also trust the folder: doctor reads its trust.json, read-only
steps.why: the guard stops a risky command, like a force push, before the agent runs it

steps.title: Add the yokoten runtime to the project
steps.how: .yokoten/VERSION is the version of the yokoten that runs doctor; yokoten's own repo needs no copy
steps.why: the hooks and CI run this copy, so they work with no network and no global install

steps.title: Run your tests on every push
steps.how: package.json has a real "test" script and a `run:` step in a workflow runs it, or a `run:` step starts a test runner such as `node --test`, `go test`, `pytest`, `tox`, `make test` or `npx vitest`; in a workspaces repo, `npm test --workspaces` or `pnpm -r test` counts too
steps.why: tests that run on every push catch a broken change before it reaches main

steps.title: Run the checks on every pull request
steps.how: a workflow in the folder this project's code host reads (`.github/workflows`, and `.gitea/workflows` too on Gitea) runs `yokoten check` (by its path, or with npx, bunx or pnpm dlx), or has a step that uses yokoten-labs/yokoten
steps.why: a commit made with the hook off would reach main unchecked

steps.title: Turn on issues
steps.how: there is no TODO.md, TODO, todo.md or docs/todo
steps.why: an issue has an owner, a state and a history; a todo file has none

steps.title: Add issue and pull request templates
steps.how: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE holds a template, and .github holds a pull request template
steps.why: a template asks for what a reviewer needs, so nothing is forgotten

steps.title: Keep build output out of git
steps.how: no tracked file is in a dist/, build/ or out/ folder or is a built file by its name, apart from yokoten.json "allowBuild"
steps.why: a build makes these files again from the source, and a reviewer can't read a binary

steps.title: Keep a changelog
steps.how: CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased heading, or the repo has a changes/ folder or a .changeset/ folder (Changesets)
steps.why: each pull request adds its entry as it goes, so a release needs no digging
steps.what: no CHANGELOG.md with an "Unreleased" section, and no changes/ folder
steps.fix: `yokoten init` adds both; then each pull request adds a file in changes/ for each change that users notice

steps.title: Check pull request titles
steps.how: a workflow in the folder this project's code host reads (`.github/workflows`, and `.gitea/workflows` too on Gitea) runs `yokoten check --pr`, or runs on pull requests with a step that uses yokoten-labs/yokoten and does not set `pr-check: false`
steps.why: a pull request title becomes the commit on main, so it must say what changed and why
steps.what: CI does not check pull requests (`yokoten check --pr`)

steps.title: Name the owner (CODEOWNERS)
steps.how: a CODEOWNERS file is in .github/, at the root or in docs/, and the first one GitHub reads names an owner, not init's placeholder @YOUR_GITHUB_HANDLE; full doctor also reads whether the repo belongs to an organization, and an organization alone (@org, not @org/team) is not an owner
steps.why: the host then asks you to review a pull request that changes those paths, and `check --pr` makes it tier A
steps.fix: `yokoten init` writes .github/CODEOWNERS for the lead-only paths; or add one with a line `<path> @<your account>` for each path where a mistake is hard to undo: the rules, CI, agent config

steps.title: Keep your agents in a sandbox
steps.how: .claude/settings.json turns the sandbox on with no * host; .codex/config.toml pins workspace-write, on-request and no network; .gemini/settings.json blocks YOLO mode; .grok/sandbox.toml holds a workspace profile; writable paths stay in the project
steps.why: a worker writes only where the sandbox allows, so it must cover the worktree

steps.title: Add a license and a security policy
steps.how: a SECURITY.md, a Dependabot config and a license file are in the repo
steps.why: people can then report a hole in private, old dependencies get updates, and others know how they may use the code
steps.fix: run `yokoten init` to add the security policy and Dependabot

name: Incident
description: "Something went wrong in how we work. The rca skill turns it into a check. Title: `area: symptom` (what you saw, not the fix), for example `check: misses a key in a JSON file`. At most 60 characters, no full stop, no #N."
title: "area: "
labels: [incident]
body:
  - type: textarea
    id: what
    attributes:
      label: What happened
      description: Facts only, in order, with times in UTC.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: matters
    attributes:
      label: Why it matters
      description: "What it cost, or can cost, when it happens again. One or two sentences. `yokoten learn` uses it as the check's reason."
  - type: textarea
    id: why
    attributes:
      label: Why it got through
      description: Which check should have caught it, and why it did not (or that there was none).
  - type: textarea
    id: fix
    attributes:
      label: Fix
      description: What changed so it can't happen again, and the check that now holds it.
  - type: textarea
    id: spread
    attributes:
      label: Other places it can happen
      description: Other projects or paths with the same gap (yokoten).

name: Task
description: "A piece of work. Every change starts here. Title: `area: verb phrase`, for example `doctor: add the review step`. At most 60 characters, no full stop, no #N."
title: "area: "
body:
  - type: textarea
    id: goal
    attributes:
      label: Goal
      description: What is true when this is done, in one or two sentences.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: done
    attributes:
      label: Done when
      description: The checks that prove it. A command and its expected output is best.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: scope
    attributes:
      label: Out of scope
      description: What this task must not change.

# Security

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please report it privately, not in a public issue. Go to this repo's **Security** tab
and choose **Report a vulnerability**. Only the maintainers see the report.

Include what you did, what happened, and what you expected. Add the version or commit
you used. Steps that show the problem help most.

## What not to put in a public issue

A public issue is open to everyone, at once. Don't put any of these in one:

- the details of a vulnerability, or how to use it;
- a password, token, key or other secret, even an old one;
- personal data about anyone.

If a secret is already public, say so in the private report. It must be revoked, not
only deleted.

## What counts

A vulnerability is a fault that lets someone do what they should not be able to do.
For example:

- run code on a machine or server that uses this project;
- read or change data they have no right to;
- get a secret, or get past a login or a permission check.

A bug that only breaks things, with no gain for an attacker, is a normal issue. Open
it in public.

<!-- yokoten kit 0.2.0 -->
# How work is done here

This file is for every agent and every person working in this repo. It starts from
[yokoten](https://github.com/yokoten-labs/yokoten)'s core rules; the project's own section is
at the end.

Every rule names why it exists and the check that holds it. A rule with no check is a
wish: the check is what makes it true on a busy day. The "why" is an **incident** when
one happened, and a **risk** when the rule came first. Incidents are never made up; a
risk becomes an incident only when it happens. When a rule here fails, use the `rca`
skill: find the cause, add or fix the check, then carry the fix to the other projects.

## Roles

- **The owner** decides what is built and when it ships. Only the owner approves a pull
  request that touches a hard line (a CODEOWNERS path, such as the release), creates release
  tags, and changes repo settings. Another tier A pull request merges once a reviewer of
  another model approves it and every check passes.
- **The lead** is the session the owner talks to. It plans, splits the work, reviews,
  commits and opens pull requests (as the bot, never as the owner).
- **A worker** is a session the lead starts for one task, in its own worktree, with
  `YOKOTEN_ROLE=worker`. It changes code and tests, and reports back. It never pushes.

## Core rules

| # | Rule | Why | Check |
|---|------|-----|-------|
| 1 | Every piece of work starts as an issue. No todo files. | Incident: follow-ups written only in chat reports were nearly lost; a shared todo file made one PR run CI four times on merge conflicts. | `doctor` reports todo files |
| 2 | Nothing reaches `main` without a pull request and green CI. | Risk: one bad push breaks every branch built on it. | Branch ruleset on the server |
| 3 | Only the owner creates tags and releases. A general "merge", "ship it" or "go ahead" does not approve a release. Only an owner request that names the version or says "release", "publish" or "tag" does. | Risk: when to ship is the owner's call, and a pushed tag can start a release. | Tool guard; tag ruleset on the server |
| 4 | A fix task changes code, never tests (`YOKOTEN_FIX_TASK=1`). | Risk: the fastest way to make a test pass is to change what it asserts. | Tool guard and commit check |
| 5 | A worker does not change lead-only files: these rules, agent config, hooks, CI. | Risk: a pull request that edits CI runs that CI before anyone reads it. | Tool guard and commit check for workers; for the bot, no Workflows permission, or CODEOWNERS review of CI changes with every secret behind a protected environment |
| 6 | Never skip the commit check (`--no-verify`, changing `core.hooksPath`). | Risk: a skipped check makes a broken commit look reviewed. | Tool guard; CI runs the same check |
| 7 | No plain force push. Merge `main` into a branch only on a real conflict; never rebase a shared branch. | Risk: a force push throws away commits someone else pushed. | Tool guard; branch ruleset |
| 8 | Squash merge. One pull request, one purpose; small polish goes in one batch. A pull request has a commit-form title, a `tier:` line, Why / What changed / How tested, a linked issue, a file in `changes/` when behaviour changes, a milestone, a type label, and a tier label that matches the `tier:` line. An issue title is `area: verb phrase` (a task) or `area: symptom` (an incident): at most 60 characters, no full stop, no `#N`. | Incident: the owner was asked to review a +3 −2 pull request on its own and said small changes should not each cost a review. | Repo settings (squash only); `check --pr` and `check --issue` in CI |
| 9 | Review and test the exact commit that merges. The reviewer only reads; the verifier runs it. | Incident: two pull requests, each green on its own, broke `main` together, twice. | `inspect` skill; merge queue where the host has one |
| 10 | No folder holds more than 7 entries (the root is not counted). | Risk: a flat folder grows until nobody can find anything. Set as a standard by the owner. | Commit check (layout) |
| 11 | Nothing in the repo, or in what yokoten prints, points at a person or opens their accounts: no personal email, IP, name, city or private domain, and no secret (token or private key). A hit is reported by place, never by content; the home folder shows as `~`. | Incident: the old check read only the live docs, and server names and addresses were still in 56 tracked files. | Commit check and CI (privacy and secrets); `check --history` before going public |
| 12 | Decisions are written down once and kept. A changed decision gets a new entry that points back. Facts are replaced, not added to. Times are UTC, commit times included. | Risk: a decision that lives only in a chat gets argued again. Incident: every commit recorded the owner's time zone (#40). | `record` skill; commit check (commit time) |

## Writing

Plain English, close to ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English), because the readers
include beginners, people reading a second language, and agents. An instruction has at
most 20 words; a description at most 25. One instruction per sentence. One word for one
thing. Active voice. A flow gets a diagram. `check --pr` notes long sentences in changed
Markdown; a note never fails CI.

## Names

A name is what a reader meets first and reads most. Pick names that a new reader, or an
agent, understands without scrolling back. The yokoten guide says why:
[Naming](https://github.com/yokoten-labs/yokoten/blob/main/docs/guide.md#naming).

- Whole words. A short form only when everyone knows it (`id`, `url`, `config`). Never
  delete letters inside a word.
- At most 4 words. There is no character limit, because a limit makes people abbreviate.
- One letter only for a name used within about 10 lines, such as a loop counter.
- A function's name starts with a verb. A true/false value starts with `is`, `has` or
  `can`.
- One idea keeps one name in every file.
- Use the language's own case style, for example `camelCase` in TypeScript and
  `snake_case` in Python.

| Hard to read | Easy to read | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `r`, still used 30 lines later | `result` | By line 30 the reader has forgotten what `r` holds. |
| `cfgMgr` | `configManager` | Letters cut from inside words make the reader guess. |
| `processTheUserInputDataNow` | `parseInput` | Six words, and three of them say nothing. |
| `valid` | `isValid` | `is` says the value is only true or false. |

## Where to look

| For | Read |
|-----|------|
| Why something is the way it is | `docs/records/` |
| Handing a task to a worker | the `dispatch` skill |
| Reviewing a pull request | the `inspect` skill |
| Something went wrong | the `rca` skill |
| What this repo is missing | `yokoten doctor` |

## This project

### Build
Python >=3.10, managed with `uv` and `pyproject.toml` (`pdm-backend`).
Install deps: `uv sync --locked --no-dev --group tests --extra all` (as in CI).
For docs: `uv sync --locked --no-dev --group docs`.
Build package: `uv build` (requires `pdm-backend`).

### Test
Run tests: `bash scripts/test.sh` (used in test-redistribute).
With coverage: `bash scripts/test-cov.sh` and `uv run coverage combine coverage` then `uv run coverage report --fail-under=100`.
Run single file: `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_*.py`.
Pre-commit checks: `uv run prek run --from-ref origin/<base> --to-ref HEAD`.

### What not to touch
Do not edit generated docs site `site/`.
Do not manually edit `uv.lock` or `pyproject.toml` dependencies unless required.
Do not change release files `fastapi/__init__.py` version and `docs/en/docs/release-notes.md` outside release flow.
TODO: Owner must confirm preferred local test command and coverage threshold.

# Changelog

All notable changes are listed here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and versions follow
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Dates are UTC.

Each pull request that changes what users see adds a file in `changes/`, not a line
here, so pull requests never conflict. `changes/README.md` shows the form. Before a
release, `node .yokoten/bin/yokoten.ts changelog --write` moves the entries under `[Unreleased]`. Then
the owner moves them under a new version heading.

## [Unreleased]
